steps.title: Social Security Registration
steps.description: Register the employee with the Eritrean Social Security Authority. Both employer and employee contribute 6% of the gross salary (total 12%).

items.title: Foreign Worker Quotas
items.text: Eritrea prioritizes local hiring. EOR for expats requires proving that no qualified local worker is available for the role.

items.title: Labour Proclamation 2001
items.text: All employment is governed by Proclamation 118/2001. Understanding the 'just cause' termination rules is critical to avoid legal disputes.

items.title: 2% Rehabilitation Tax
items.text: Many Eritreans globally pay a 2% rehabilitation tax; while usually personal, ensure your payroll policy accounts for any local obligations.

items.title: Medical Coverage

faqs.question: Can I hire expats via EOR in Eritrea?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it requires a work permit. The EOR provider acts as the local sponsor. Expect 4-8 weeks for permit processing.

faqs.question: What is the maximum probation period?
faqs.answer: Under Eritrean law, probation is typically limited to 45 days. Any extension requires documentation of performance issues.

faqs.question: Who owns the intellectual property?
faqs.answer: Contracts are drafted to ensure that all IP created by the employee is assigned to the client company, not the EOR provider.

faqs.question: What is the notice period?
faqs.answer: Notice periods range from 7 days to 2 months depending on length of service as prescribed in Proclamation 118/2001.

items.title: Currency Controls
items.text: Eritrea has strict exchange controls. Pay in local Nakfa (ERN) is mandatory for local residents; foreign currency accounts require specific authorization.

items.title: Social Security Deadline
items.text: Contributions must be paid within 15 days after the month's end. Late payments incur a 2% monthly penalty.

items.title: Overtime Rates
items.text: Ensure overtime is calculated correctly: 1.25x for day (6am-10pm), 1.5x for night, and 2.5x for public holidays.

faqs.question: Is there a 13th month salary requirement?
faqs.answer: No, a 13th-month bonus is not legally mandated in Eritrea, though it is a common practice for some NGOs and international firms.

faqs.question: What are the standard working hours?
faqs.answer: The law allows for 8 hours per day, totaling 40 or 48 hours per week depending on the industry agreement.

faqs.question: Are digital payslips allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, but many local employees may still require paper copies for banking and housing purposes.

faqs.question: How long does it take to register a company?

faqs.question: Can a foreigner own 100% of a company?

faqs.question: Do I need a physical office?
faqs.answer: Yes, a registered physical address in Eritrea is mandatory for the trade license application.
